question_tree.question: Is the RAM stick fully clicked into the slot (you hear a click and clips are locked)?

next.text: Reseat the RAM: power off, unplug, press the stick firmly until both side clips lock. Then power on.

next.question: Have you tried the RAM in a different slot on the motherboard?

next.text: Try a different DIMM slot — this isolates whether it's a slot or stick issue.

options.answer: Yes, same issue in other slots

next.question: Does the motherboard have a debug LED or beep code for RAM errors?

options.answer: Yes, RAM LED is lit / beeping

next.text: Likely faulty RAM stick or incompatible RAM. Test with a single known-good stick, then check the motherboard QVL (compatibility list) for your RAM.
This may be a motherboard or CPU issue beyond basic checks — recommend professional diagnosis.

question_tree.question: Did the blue screen start right after adding or swapping RAM sticks?

next.question: Are all installed sticks the exact same speed and timing (check labels)?

next.text: Mismatched RAM (different speed/timing/brand) can cause instability. Run each stick individually to confirm, then either match kits or set speed manually in BIOS to the slowest stick's rated speed.
Enable XMP/EXPO in BIOS if not already on, or run at JEDEC default speed as a stability test. Also run MemTest86 for at least one full pass to rule out a faulty stick.

options.answer: No, it started later / unrelated timing

next.text: This is likely a software/driver issue rather than RAM — recommend checking Windows Event Viewer for the specific BSOD stop code, or professional diagnosis if crashes continue.

title: System won't boot after installing new RAM

question_tree.question: Do you get any power (fans spin, lights on) when you press the power button?

next.text: This points to a PSU or motherboard power issue, not RAM specifically — recommend professional diagnosis.

options.answer: Yes, power comes on but no boot/display

next.question: Is the new RAM on the motherboard's QVL (Qualified Vendor List) for your board?

next.text: Check your motherboard manufacturer's QVL page for your exact RAM model. Unlisted kits sometimes need a BIOS update to be recognized.
Update your motherboard BIOS to the latest version — QVL-listed RAM sometimes needs a newer BIOS to be detected correctly, especially on AM5/LGA1700 boards.

title: PC overheating / thermal throttling after RAM change

question_tree.question: Did you increase RAM speed or enable XMP/EXPO around the same time the overheating started?

next.text: Higher RAM speeds can slightly increase VRM/chipset heat on some boards. Check chipset temps in BIOS/HWiNFO; ensure case airflow covers the VRM area, and confirm RAM voltage isn't set above the kit's rated spec.
Overheating unrelated to RAM changes is most likely CPU cooler, thermal paste, or case airflow — outside RAM scope, recommend a full thermal check.

question_tree.question: Are you able to see bent, broken, or missing pins in the DIMM slot with the stick removed?

next.text: Physically damaged DIMM slots require professional repair or motherboard replacement — do not force a stick into a damaged slot.

options.answer: No visible damage, but suspect it's bad

next.text: Test a known-good RAM stick in that specific slot alone. If it's still not detected while other slots work fine with the same stick, the slot itself is likely the fault — note this for a replacement/repair quote.
